engineering_objective: Complete the inherited ansibleops Terraform provider so its ten Ansible-backed operating-system resources behave as normal managed Terraform resources with Terraform-owned durable state, native drift reconciliation, safe lifecycle transitions, and deterministic local execution.
required_end_state: The provider exposes the documented ten resources as real Terraform managed resources; repeated apply/plan/refresh cycles converge against local Linux reality, resource identity remains stable across in-place changes, failures do not corrupt Terraform state, deletes affect only owned objects, and Ansible execution is deterministic and failure-safe.
functional_requirements: Keep exactly the ten documented ansibleops managed resource types functional through the Terraform Plugin Framework, with Terraform Core as the durable state owner and no provider-owned state database.
Derive each resource identity only from its documented external object key so mutable metadata, content, targets, variables, schedules, or account attributes update in place without identity churn.
Use Ansible for Create, Update, and Delete mutations, while Read/refresh observes native Linux state without invoking ansible-playbook.
During refresh, treat a missing or wrong-kind owned object as absent and refresh externally changed managed values so Terraform plans reconciliation rather than accepting stale prior state.
For file, directory, and symlink resources, preserve documented path/type/metadata semantics; deleting a symlink must remove only the link path and never its target.

For copy and template resources, treat source_digest as caller-supplied source-content intent, observe destination content, and make template variable handling deterministic regardless of map ordering.

For line and block resources, manage the documented named contract idempotently: updates must not accumulate duplicates, Read must be side-effect free, and delete must remove only the owned line or block.
For user and group resources, observe the native account/group databases, normalize supplementary groups deterministically, and honor remove_home_on_destroy exactly for user deletion.
For cron resources, manage one named entry, default an omitted user to root and omitted schedule fields to wildcards, preserve sibling entries, and converge cleanly after apply.

Publish new Terraform resource state only after a successful mutation; non-zero exits, timeout, or cancellation must fail the transition without advancing applied state, and a later retry must be able to converge.

Execute ansible-playbook with structured arguments rather than shell interpolation so valid paths containing spaces or shell metacharacters remain literal, and clean generated temporary playbooks after success and failure paths.
Normalize semantically equivalent modes, unordered values, ownership/account observations, and cron defaults so repeated clean plan/refresh cycles are stable and do not replay Ansible.
preservation_requirements: Preserve the provider source address local/ansibleops, provider version 0.1.0, existing Plugin Framework entrypoint, and the documented ten resource interfaces under /app/provider.
Preserve Terraform Core as the only durable state authority; do not introduce a provider-owned durable database or manually create or edit terraform.tfstate.
Preserve solver-visible provider, resource, and lifecycle documentation as the technical contract surface unless a genuine contract correction is required.
compatibility_requirements: The repaired provider must remain buildable with the task's Go 1.24 toolchain and current Terraform Plugin Framework dependency set.
The provider must continue to operate with the local managed inventory at /app/provider/config/inventory.ini and the existing local provider installation layout.
Keep normal Terraform apply, plan, refresh, destroy, and state inspection semantics compatible with Terraform CLI 1.10.5 used by the task environment.
safety_requirements: Do not replace the managed resources with null_resource, terraform_data execution wrappers, local-exec, remote-exec, or other Terraform provisioner substitutes.
Do not use shell command interpolation for ansible-playbook invocation; paths and user-controlled values must remain structured data.
Failed Update or Delete operations must not claim successful external transitions in Terraform state.
Deletion of line, block, cron, symlink, and user resources must remain scoped to their documented ownership boundaries, including preserving a user's home unless remove_home_on_destroy is true.
Generated Ansible playbooks are ephemeral and must not accumulate after success, non-zero exit, timeout, or cancellation; diagnostics must not persist full command output in Terraform state.

required_outputs.notes: Repair the inherited provider source in place. The verifier rebuilds and exercises this artifact.
